bottom_line: In this trial, there was no significant difference between bolus every 12 hours vs continuous infusion in patients’ global assessment of symptoms (mean AUC, 4236±1440 and 4373±1404, respectively; P = 0.47) or change in creatinine from baseline to 72 hours (0.05±0.3 mg per deciliter and 0.07±0.3 mg per deciliter, respectively; P = 0.45).
implications: These data support that, over 72 hours, bolus vs continuous infusion did not differ on the coprimary endpoints (global symptom AUC 4236±1440 vs 4373±1404; creatinine change 0.05±0.3 vs 0.07±0.3 mg per deciliter). For high-dose vs low-dose, the symptom AUC difference did not meet conventional statistical significance (P = 0.06), while worsening renal function within 72 hours was more frequent with high-dose (23% vs 14%; P = 0.04); the trial also states it was not powered to detect between-group differences in clinical events.
